pages.text: In the evening, boats returned to the harbor one by one. Riri and Lolo went to the pier.
They wanted to spot Dad's boat first. Mom said, "Seagulls always follow behind Dad's boat."
Riri climbed the stone steps. Lolo ran to the end of the long seawall. "We should look from up high." "We should look from close by."
Riri inspected the boats one at a time. This boat belonged to someone else, and so did that one.
Riri spent a long time studying one boat. Meanwhile, other boats passed far ahead.
Lolo waved at every approaching boat. "Dad!"
A stranger waved back. Lolo quietly lowered both hands.
A flock of seagulls arrived, crying overhead. A boat came in beneath them.
Dad stood at the bow, waving both arms wide. It was Dad's boat!
"I saw it first!" "I saw it first!" They shouted together. "But these fellows got here first!" Dad pointed at the seagulls on the boat's roof.
